This setup creates conditions favorable for total internal reflection of light from distant objects. Consider a ray, OA, from a distant object. As it passes through each layer of air, it bends away from the normal due to refraction. Eventually, when the angle of incidence reaches the critical angle, the ray undergoes total internal reflection, moving upward along AB. This phenomenon creates an illusion where the distant object appears to be reflected as if it were over a body of water. An observer at point B sees the image of the object just below its actual position, accompanied by a portion of the sky surrounding it. This optical illusion mimics the appearance of an object reflected in water, creating what we perceive as a mirage. Sample Questions: 1. Can total internal reflection be achieved if an objet originates in rarer medium? 15.7 Applications of Total Internal Reflection a. Optical Fiber:

An optical fiber is a device based on total internal reflection. With the use of an optical fiber, a light signal can be transmitted from one place to another with a negligible loss of energy. It is a very long and Physics, Grade 11 | 330

thin pipe (thickness nearly 10–4 m) of a transparent material with a double layer such that the outer layer has a relatively lower refractive index. Large number of such fibers is held together from a light pipe. Optical fibers are used for the signal for communication. A ray of light strikes from one end at a small angle of incidence so that firstly it suffers refraction and then multiple total internal reflections and finally strikes the other end at an angle less than the critical angle. As a result, the ray emerges out in air as shown in figure 15.7. There is no loss of energy during total internal reflection. The optical fiber is used in light pipe. The application of the principle of total internal reflection in optical fibers has revolutionized communication field, medical field, and optical examinations field. Furthermore, the optical fiber has numerous applications as listed below. i) Telecommunications:

Optical fibers are extensively used in telecommunications networks to transmit voice, data, and video signals. High-speed and long-distance communication, telephone systems, and cable television are possible with the use of optical fibers. Optical fiber facilitates provide seamless online activities, streaming, and large file transfer. ii) Medical Imaging:
Optical fibers have a crucial role in medical imaging fields, such as endoscopy and fiber optic microscopy. Endoscopes use flexible light pipe to visualize internal organs. iii) Data Centers:

Optical fibers are extensively used in data centers for interconnecting servers. They are also used in storage systems and networking equipments. They make rapid transmission of large volumes of data possible.

The critical angle for diamond-air interface is very small, nearly 24.4. Therefore, for most of the cases, when light from an external source enters in a well cut diamond, it suffers multiple total internal reflection inside the diamond. In such situations light entering into diamond from all directions finally emerges out from some particular directions. Therefore, while looking from those directions, the diamond appears sparkling. A diamond cutter utilizes this principle so that multiple total internal reflections occur and sparkling of diamonds becomes possible.
